title: Integrated rover v2 with front drum and high-lift dump
problem_restatement: Build a 60 kg 1.0x0.5x0.5 m rover that traverses loose BP-1, digs and carries soil, sees and stops safely without line-of-sight, runs on onboard power, resists dust and heat, and dumps over a 1.0 m bin without tipping.
mechanism_sentence: Wide wheels roll over loose soil while a front drum scoops soil into a middle bin that climbs to 1.05 m to pour into a tall box.
decisive_choices: Choose 4-wheel drive rigid grouser wheels over tracked skid-steer to float on BP-1
Choose front transverse bucket drum over rear bucket ladder to keep belly clear
Choose rear high-lift mast with dual 500 N actuators to lift pour lip to 1.05 m to clear 1.0 m bin over tilt-only dump
open_question: Does 2.92 kg for 1 kWh implying 342 Wh per kg recompute to a realistic pack mass and 30-min energy versus 341 W and 50.6 kg total?
transfer_line: Load: front bucket drum -> central hopper -> high-lift mast | Measured: depth camera -> dual-link teleoperation

assumed_constraints.constraint: Stay within 60 kg mass and 1.0 x 0.5 x 0.5 m size limits
Clear 1.0 m high collection bin lip to dump by gravity
Carry 10 kg BP-1 load at loose density near 0.90 g per cm3
Size 24 V pack for 30 min digging sortie at hundreds of watts

functional_decomposition: Traverse loose BP-1 bed without immobilization
Excavate and lift BP-1 into onboard carrying volume
React digging forces within 60 kg and 1.0x0.5x0.5 m limits
Provide remote situational awareness without line-of-sight
Maintain safe remote link with independent stop
Supply onboard power for drive digging computing and lighting
Protect electronics from dust intrusion and thermal overload
Store BP-1 onboard and dump into collection bin without spillage or tipping

concept.working_principle: Four rigid grouser wheels carry a low frame over BP-1, a front bucket drum scoops soil into a central hopper, and a rear high-lift mast raises the hopper pivot to 1.05 m to clear the 1.0 m bin lip for gravity pouring, powered by a 24 V pack in a sealed box with an elevated sensor mast for out-of-sight driving and heartbeat stop-and-hold.

fabrication_steps.description: Assemble the low aluminum tube frame with belly pan about 0.95 m long
Mount the four 300 mm rigid wheels and the front bucket drum
Fit the central hopper on the rear high-lift mast with dual actuators
Install the battery pack, sealed electronics box and tilting sensor mast on top

risks.risk: Battery mass 2.92 kg for 1 kWh implies 342 Wh per kg outside everyday scale
risks.mitigation: Recompute pack mass at near 100 Wh per kg and 30-min energy versus 341 W and joint total

risks.risk: Lift travel plausible but actuator force proof failed
risks.mitigation: Show linkage force with friction for dual 500 N actuators through 4 to 1 chain to 1.05 m lip

novelty_claim: Front bucket drum feeding central hopper lifted on rear high-lift mast to pour over tall bin

figure_spec.system_view: Side view of low tube frame with central hopper on rear high-lift mast raised to dump over 1.0 m bin lip

open_questions: Does 2.92 kg for 1 kWh implying 342 Wh per kg recompute to a realistic pack mass and 30-min energy versus 341 W and 50.6 kg total?
Does 150 mm stroke through 4 to 1 linkage provide enough force with friction to lift 10 kg to 1.05 m pour lip?
O1: Missing mass integration and dump stability proof

O2: Dump kinematics and tip moment unproven: 0.45 m stowed frame to clear 1.0 m bin lip with 150 mm stroke 500 N actuator and 0.50 m hopper, plus tip factor 7.1 looks high versus wheelbarrow experience. Sam to show pivot geometry and moment arms.
O4: Battery mass 2.92 kg for ~1 kWh LiFePO4 implies >300 Wh/kg, outside everyday pack scale; Priya to recompute mass and 30-min energy vs E34 and E50 before vote.
